# Pi runtime reference

This reference applies to adopters using the Pi target. For daily render and check usage, see
[Working with awf](working-with-awf.md); general task capabilities come from the separately
installed [agentic-skills](https://github.com/hypnotox/agentic-skills) package.

## Prerequisites and ownership

Install `pi-tools` globally using its own supported installation instructions, then install
`agentic-skills` for Pi. The external package supplies the seven generic `agentic-*` skills,
canonical role prompts, and the thin role-registration adapter. `pi-tools` supplies role execution,
model selection, scheduling, tool policy, and other runtime mechanics.

AWF neither installs, vendors, updates, configures, nor probes either dependency. The AWF binary and
its render, check, initialization, and upgrade operations remain usable offline when neither global
package is present. Missing generic skills or role delegation is an operator installation issue, not
AWF drift.

The Pi target renders only the four repository-local skills `awf-effort`, `awf-topics`,
`awf-decisions`, and `awf-maintenance` under `.pi/skills/`. Their names do not use the configured
project prefix. AWF renders no role prompts, subagent extension, model router, role policy, model
preference file, or tool registration. Repository-local and globally installed skills therefore
coexist without naming or registration collisions.

## Session continuity

Before work continues in another session at a safe resumable checkpoint, resolve the effort memory
path with `./awf effort show <slug>` and update that Markdown under the one-writer rule. The successor
uses `agentic-context` to reorient from repository authority before substantive work. Managed
worktree use ends before integration, deferred lifecycle closure, worktree removal, optional
durable-lesson capture, and final effort closure. AWF owns this continuity guidance and provides no
executable handoff implementation.
